title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study)

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study). Part 1.1 - level A1-A2 - scored items 1, 2 and 3. The examiner asks you three short questions about yourself, one after another. You have 30 seconds to answer each question. There is NO preparation time. Begin speaking when you hear the sound.

questions.q:
TEST: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study)
PART 1.1 - level A1-A2 - scored items 1-3 - exchanging personal information.
Timing: 30 seconds for each question. No preparation time.

WHOLE PAPER AT A GLANCE (examiner, read this before you start; do NOT read it to the candidate):
  Part 1.1 - A1-A2 - 3 questions - scored items 1, 2, 3 - 30 seconds each - no preparation.
  Part 1.2 - B1  - 2 pictures + 3 questions - scored items 4, 5, 6 - 45s / 30s / 30s - no preparation.
  Part 2   - B2  - 1 picture + 3 questions together - scored item 7 - 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking.
  Part 3   - C1  - 1 topic statement with a FOR list and an AGAINST list - scored item 8 - 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking.
  Marks: items 1-3 = 0-5; items 4-6 = 0-5; item 7 = 0-5; item 8 = 0-6. Maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75.
  Run the four parts back to back without a break. The conversion table is printed in the Part 3 instructions.

[EXAMINER READS ALOUD, word for word:]
"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound."

[STAGE DIRECTION: play the chime. Then ask the three questions one after another. Allow exactly 30 seconds for each answer. If the candidate stops early, wait a moment and then move on; if the candidate is still speaking at 30 seconds, say "Thank you" politely and go straight to the next question. Do not rephrase the questions, do not add prompts, and do not comment on the answers.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds) - [chime]
"Tell me about your studies or your job. What do you study, or what work do you do?"

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds) - [chime]
"How do you usually get to your school, your college or your workplace in the morning?"

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds) - [chime]
"What time of day do you like studying or working best, and why?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: after the third answer say "Thank you." and go straight on to the two photographs in Part 1.2. Do not announce a new part to the candidate - for the candidate, Part 1.1 and Part 1.2 are both "part one".]

[EXAMINER MARKING NOTE: items 1-3 are marked together, 0-5.]

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study). Part 1.2 - level B1 - scored items 4, 5 and 6. You will see two photographs on one theme. The examiner asks you three questions, one after another. Question 4 (comparing the two photographs) - 45 seconds. Questions 5 and 6 (your opinion) - 30 seconds each. There is NO preparation time.

questions.q:
TEST: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study)
PART 1.2 - level B1 - scored items 4-6 - describing, giving a personal opinion and justifying it.
Timing: question 4 = 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 = 30 seconds each. No preparation time.

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the candidate the two photographs side by side. If no photographs have been attached in Test bazasi, read the two descriptions below aloud, slowly and clearly, before asking question 4.]

[PICTURE 1: a bright open-plan office in the middle of the morning. Five colleagues of mixed ages stand around a high table covered with laptops, printed charts and coloured sticky notes. One woman is pointing at a whiteboard while the others listen and one of them writes; coats hang on a rail behind them and tall windows show a busy city street outside.]

[PICTURE 2: a small bedroom late at night. A young man sits alone at a narrow desk under a single lamp, a thick textbook open in front of him and handwritten notes pinned to the wall above it. A cold cup of tea and a face-down phone lie beside the book, and the rest of the room is in darkness.]

[EXAMINER READS ALOUD, word for word:]
"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

QUESTION 4 (45 seconds) - [chime] - this is the compare-and-describe question, and it is the question you have just read out: "Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"
[STAGE DIRECTION: no preparation time. Allow 45 seconds. If the candidate describes only one photograph, you may prompt once: "And the other picture?" Say "Thank you" at 45 seconds and move straight on.]

QUESTION 5 (30 seconds) - [chime]
"Which of these two ways of working - together with other people, or alone - helps a person to get more done? Why do you think so?"

QUESTION 6 (30 seconds) - [chime]
"Some people study or work late at night, like the man in the second picture. Do you think that is a good idea? Why, or why not?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: questions 5 and 6 follow one after another with no preparation time, 30 seconds each. After the third answer say "Thank you. That is the end of part one." Do not comment on the content of the answers.]

[EXAMINER MARKING NOTE: items 4-6 are marked together, 0-5.]

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study). Part 2 - level B2 - scored item 7. You will see one picture and three questions, all at the same time. You are NOT required to describe the picture - it is only there to introduce the topic. You have 1 minute to think about your answers, and then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together.

questions.q:
TEST: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study)
PART 2 - level B2 - scored item 7 - reasoning on an abstract topic, weighing advantages and drawbacks and justifying them.
Timing: 1 minute preparation, then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together.

[EXAMINER READS ALOUD, word for word:]
"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound. Look at the photograph."

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the picture and the three questions AT THE SAME TIME, and leave them in front of the candidate for the whole task. If no photograph has been attached in Test bazasi, read the description below aloud.]

[PICTURE: a college training workshop in the afternoon. A woman of about thirty-five, in protective overalls and safety glasses, is being shown how to wire an electrical panel by an instructor who is guiding her hand. Around her, students ten or fifteen years younger work at similar benches. Her handbag and a folder of college papers rest on a stool behind her.]

[EXAMINER ADDS, once, then reads the three questions aloud in order before the preparation minute begins:]
"You do not need to describe the picture. It is only there to introduce the topic. Here are your three questions."

THE THREE QUESTIONS (shown together, answered together within the two minutes):
1. "Tell me about a skill you have learned outside school or university."
2. "How has learning that skill changed the way you study or work?"
3. "What do you think influences people most when they decide to train for a completely new kind of work?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: give exactly 1 minute of silence for preparation; the candidate may make notes. After 60 seconds say "Your minute is up," play the chime and time 2 minutes. Do not interrupt between the questions. If the candidate stops well before two minutes, wait about ten seconds and then say, once only, "Is there anything else you would like to add?" At 2 minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of part two."]

[EXAMINER MARKING NOTE: item 7 is marked 0-5. The candidate is NOT required to describe the picture, so do not take marks off for leaving it out; but a candidate who only describes the picture and does not answer the three questions cannot be given the top mark.]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study). Part 3 - level C1 - scored item 8. You will see a topic on the screen with two lists of points beside it, FOR and AGAINST. Choose TWO points from EACH list and give a balanced argument representing both sides of the topic. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak.

EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING OF THE SPEAKING PAPER: items 1-3 together = 0-5; items 4-6 together = 0-5; item 7 (Part 2) = 0-5; item 8 (Part 3) = 0-6. Maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75.

questions.q:
TEST: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant B (Work and Study)
PART 3 - level C1 - scored item 8 - reasoning on an abstract topic, analysing both sides.
Timing: 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking.

[EXAMINER READS ALOUD, word for word:]
"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound."

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the topic and both lists together, or read them aloud once, slowly. Leave them in front of the candidate for the whole task.]

TOPIC STATEMENT:
"Employers should value practical work experience more highly than university qualifications."

FOR (three points):
1. Experience proves that a person can really do the job, not simply talk about it.
2. Skills learned at work stay current, while much of the content of a degree can be out of date within a few years.
3. Judging people by experience opens good careers to those who cannot afford years of full-time study.

AGAINST (three points):
1. A degree trains people to research, to read critically and to solve problems they have never met before.
2. Experience gained inside one company can be narrow, while a recognised qualification means the same thing to every employer.
3. In fields such as medicine, law and engineering, learning only on the job would be unsafe and is not permitted.

[EXAMINER REMINDER TO THE CANDIDATE, said once before the preparation minute:]
"Remember: choose two points from the 'for' list and two points from the 'against' list, and give both sides."

[STAGE DIRECTION: give exactly 1 minute of silent preparation; notes are allowed. Then play the chime and time 2 minutes. Do not interrupt and do not ask follow-up questions. At 2 minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]

[EXAMINER MARKING NOTE: item 8 is marked 0-6. A candidate who argues only one side, or who uses fewer than two points from each list, cannot be given the top mark. Whole paper: items 1-3 = 0-5, items 4-6 = 0-5, item 7 = 0-5, item 8 = 0-6; maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75 using the conversion table given in the instructions for this part.]
